cues.text: Circuit switching reserves resources for a session.
Packet switching shares links among packets, so delay can vary.
Virtual-circuit switching establishes a logical path without necessarily reserving a dedicated physical circuit.
An Ethernet switch learns the source MAC address and ingress port within each VLAN.
If the destination is known, it forwards to that port.
Unknown unicast and broadcast are flooded within the VLAN except the incoming port, and learned entries age out.
A switch does not inherently route between IP subnets.
Store-and-forward receives the full frame and can check its frame check sequence.
Cut-through starts earlier but can forward corrupt frames.
Spanning Tree Protocol blocks redundant layer two paths to prevent loops.
Link aggregation uses compatible links and, where configured, LACP; it does not necessarily multiply one flow's speed.
A virtual LAN creates a separate layer two broadcast domain.
Access ports carry one untagged VLAN.
An IEEE eight oh two dot one Q trunk carries multiple tagged VLANs, with platform-specific native or untagged handling.
To communicate across VLANs you need routing through a router subinterface or a layer three switch VLAN interface.
And remember, segmentation is not sufficient access control: inter-VLAN traffic still needs an ACL or firewall policy.
